rationale: Evidence: iteration 3 (ki 0.4, otherwise identical to iteration 1) scored 52.8064 against 52.8232 for iteration 1. Every track is essentially unchanged: rms_error is 0.0286 to 0.0300 m, max_error is 0.061 to 0.065 m, and there is one line-loss event per trial with 0 completions. The bias hypothesis (a fixed left/right motor mismatch that ki would cancel) is therefore not supported. Following the Evaluator's rule (b), I revert ki to 0 and test kd 0.15 as the single change against the best raced design. The geometry is unchanged from iteration 1 (five sensors at x = +0.03, +0.015, 0, -0.015, -0.03, y = 0.03, 16 mm footprints), because the outer-sensor reach test is still the most credible explanation for the first line loss. Changing only kd tests whether the transient after the first line loss is damping-limited. Expected result: max_error falls toward or below 0.06 m and line_loss_events drops to 0 or 1 on some seeds. If max_error and line-loss count stay the same, damping is not the limit either. The next hypotheses are then base_speed too high for the bend entry (test 1.2 to 1.3 with kd 0.15) or the line_loss recovery direction (test search_right). Measurements requested: rms_error, max_error and line_loss_events to see whether kd changes the transient; steering_oscillation to check that the extra damping does not add jitter; completion and completion_time to see whether any run finishes.
